th-grid: The level system is IndefR.Links.LevCh with LevCh.Is mu0, whose field C is a Host.CharFrame; the theta grid is ChiGrid.GridData (Places, Chars, Vertices); the grid Weil datum is GridData.Weil. Every field of LevCh, LevCh.Is and CharFrame is stated, one item per group of fields. (L1) is C.P (PiBar: pb, pb_over) and C.W (Omg: om, gen); P_g is LevCh.Pg, which LevCh.Is.Pg makes the set of places PP of E with PiBar.Div k PP (PP.under K = pb k) for some k. (L2) is C.mu0 with C.isMu0 j : IsMu0 C.P C.W (eExp D j) j, 0-based, so that C.mu0 j is mu^0_{j+1}: unitary; triv (HChar.TrivOn F); inf (HasInfQ embPsi (-eExp D j), the exponent -2 e_{j+1}(tau) at embPsi (eTau tau) = embTau tau, with eExp D j (eTau tau) = (D.hc tau).e j); unr at the places containing neither g 0 nor g 1 (OverP); tame (LevelLe 1 at every place); and atg: at the places w over pb k, locK w a = (om k a ^ (2 (j + 1)))^-1 for natural numbers a prime to g k. (L3) is C.eta with C.isEta : IsEtaT (unitary, unr, res = ResEta F, inf = HasInf embPsi 1), C.chiPsi with C.isChi : IsChiPsi (unitary, unr, triv, inf = HasInf embPsi 2), and C.del, C.del' with C.isDel : IsDelta pde and C.isDel' : IsDelta pde' (fin, triv, tame, unr at the places not over p, and ine: at a place over p, for every natural number n, del(x)^n = 1 for all units x if and only if 15 divides n, so the restriction to the units has order 15). (L4) is LevCh.xiH with LevCh.Is.xi_fin, xi_triv, xi_tame, xi_inj and xi_base; mu_{t,j} is LevCh.mu t j = Lift.tup mu0 (xi t) j = mu0 j * xi t. (L5) is LevCh.Q with LevCh.Is.Q_ram, Q_pl (IsTwistPlaces D.host.g: the residue field of PP has prime cardinality q, q is not in PP^2 and q != g k; and not IsConjPl PP PP' for PP, PP' in Q t, PP' = PP included), Q_off ((condN * D.sp.T : O_E) is not in PP, with condN = QS q d and D.sp.T the prime T of the system of spaces, and (D.mem u).A.T, the prime T_u, is not in PP for every word u; as PP is prime, this is the book's list) and Q_de. (L6) is LevCh.chi and LevCh.xiR with LevCh.Is.chi (IsRes (C.mu0 j) PP (LevCh.chi (j + 1) PP)^-1 for PP in Pg) and LevCh.Is.xiR (IsRes (xiH t) PP (xiR t PP) for PP in Q t), where IsRes chi PP c says that c (a mod PP) = chi.locK PP a for every a in O_E outside PP; LevCh.chi and xiR are given at every place and constrained only at these. (L7) is ΛY, ΛX, ΛV, ΛW with βY, βX, βV, βW and LevCh.Is.βY (for j < m, with N = g 0 * g 1), βX, βV and βW (with N = 1): IsSDFrame S β Λ N is IsBaseFrame S β Λ (N^c) for some c, that is IsFrame β Λ (the closure hatL Λ is β times the integral vectors), dualL Λ = Λ, and N^c L0c is in Λ and N^c Λ in L0c, where L0c is the lattice L_0 of the space in the coordinates of its basis; for N = 1 this makes Λ = L0c. ΛY j is a field for every j and constrained for j < m only; V_i and W_i are Vc D (i - 1) = D.sp.V i and Wc D (i - 1) = D.sp.W i. The level system's unitary characters LevCh.mu0 (j + 1), LevCh.eta and LevCh.xi t of the ideles are tied to C.mu0 j, C.eta and xiH t by LevCh.Is.mu0, eta and xi (ChrEq: continuous and trivial on E^x, and equal to the Hecke character at every finite place on the image of E^x), and the book writes mu^0_{j+1}, eta_L and xi_t for both. Spaces, ranks and signatures are Vertices.V_is, P_is and X_is (LSp.IsV: rank, SigOK, signature and IsSelfDualC) with rankV, rankP and rankX; X_is gives the signature (rankX j, 0) of (4). The embeddings are dec0 (Y_0 in P_0), colDec i (P_i in V_{i,0}), rowDecS j for 1 <= j < m (Q_j in V_{m,j}; for j = 0 the embedding is colDec m, which is GridData.rowDec 0) and topDec (V_{m,m} in Q_m), each a HermitianOrthogonalExtensionData A B c eps: an isometric embedding iota and a matrix a of c columns orthogonal to iota(A) with Gram matrix antiDiagonalSignGramMatrix c eps (1 on the antidiagonal off the diagonal, eps at its middle), with eps = 1 for dec0 and topDec and eps = -1 for colDec and rowDecS. The lattices of the embeddings are lat0, colLat, rowLat and topLat: HermitianOrthogonalExtensionData.lat is sumLat, iota(Λ) + sum_p I_p a_p, with I_p = 1 for lat0 and topLat, I_p = stairId a a' c p = a^(c - p) (a'^(p + 1))^-1 (0-based p, the book's I_{p+1}) with (a, a') = (Places.stA sc, Places.stAbar sc) = (AA * modulBar^-1, AAbar * modul^-1) for colLat, and with (a, a') = (AA, AAbar) for rowLat; Host.AA = ccE * b^-1 is the book's ideal of the host. The constants are ChiGrid.Consts (cGap, cDep, b) = (c, C_F, b). The places are ChiGrid.Places (Definition th-grid-places), which uses only Pg and Q of the level system, with S0 = insert v0 (S1 D) (Places.S0). The characters are ChiGrid.Chars pl cGap, all of whose fields are stated, for 1 <= i <= m: chi i, a circle-valued character of the ideles, and the Hecke character chiH i are tied by chi_eq (ChrEq: chi i is continuous and trivial on E^x, and agrees with chiH i at every finite place on the image of E^x), and the book writes chi_i for both; the conditions are on chiH i. (a) is triv, HChar.TrivOn F: at each place of F the product of the components at the places above it is trivial on F^x, which the book writes as triviality on A_F^x, as it does for the xi_t of the level system (LevCh.Is.xi_triv). (b) is inf, HChar.HasInf (embTau D) (2 * cen D cGap tau i), a condition on chiH i at the image of E^x in the archimedean ideles; cen D C tau i is the centre c_i(tau) of Definition th-grid-centres (floor of GridData.mid i of ofHCParam (D.hc tau) (sLen D) (gap D C) 0). The grid pairs are ChiGrid.Pair T: chi i j is (G1), mu t i j is (G2), core i is (G3) and top t j is (G4), with the ranges of Pair.InRange m; their spaces are GridData.pS and pT, the first space of chi i j and core i being negSp. c_p is GridData.chr p: G.ch.chi (m - i) for chi and core, LevCh.mu t (j + 1) for mu and top. The characters are GridData.chrS p and chrT p = Lift.attChr (chr p) LevCh.eta n, which is chr p * eta^-1 for n odd and chr p for n even, at the ranks n of pS p and pT p; chr_core shows that both are chi_{m-i} for the core pairs, the ranks of the P_i being even, and chr_mu_zero that at i = 0 they are Lift.chrStep (LevCh.mu t) eta (j + 1). th-rallis-inner-product: Standard. Proved in Alpöge's proof from ThetaLocalInputs (Chapter 12, lit-bundle-theta) by the doubling method and the Siegel-Weil formula. Relation to the literature: a special case of the Rallis inner product formula, for the theta lift of the trivial representation of a definite U(a) to a definite U(a+a') with a > a', for the test vectors of a bottom triple, with an unspecified nonzero constant c that absorbs local zeta integrals and volumes.

Archimedean data are the Lean's Fr: signs epsilon and a matrix fr with fr^* J fr equal to the Gram matrix at tau; the Cartan involution is cart and the orthonormal basis onb = fr^{-1}. Part (2) is HasInfExp. Part (4) is SquareComm.IsMatch with IsIrred and IsCoinvMap; the Lean's coinvariant maps are linear maps on all functions whose conditions concern only the span algF, and the book restricts them to that span. The proofs of parts (2) to (4) of Lemma th-square-model and of Lemma th-bottom-split-matching, on which (2) to (4) and (6) rest, are written out.

th-howe-finite: On the path used for Lemma th-square-model, the Lean does not assume Howe duality at the finite places: it proves this statement as UpperTheory.Lit.HoweDuality.sphTri, which is PositivityTheory.Sph.sphTri_of sphSplit_geo (vacInert howeInert). Alternative (1) is Sph.IrrAt and alternative (2) is Sph.SphAt (IsSph, with fields gen and line). The finite places of F are unramified in E, and the characters of a triple are unramified at the places outside its finite set, which consists of places split in E. At the inert places, howeInert proves Howe's description of the unramified Weil representation [How79] (Sph.IsHowe: the vacuum is fixed by the maximal compact subgroups of both groups, and the vectors fixed by the maximal compact subgroup of one group are spanned by the translates of the vacuum under the other), and vacInert deduces (2) with s the vacuum and the h_i in the maximal compact subgroup. At the split places, where the pairs are of type (GL_n, GL_m) (compare [Min08]), sphSplit_geo gives (1) or (2), through KCoNarrow.irrSt_narrow applied to BernsteinRamification.Close.narrowBern and latSt. The published theorem, conjectured by Howe [How89] and proved by Waldspurger for p odd [Wal90] and by Gan and Takeda for all p [GT16], says that for every irreducible smooth representation pi of U(V)(F_v) the space Theta(pi) with S_v/(pi-coinvariants) = pi tensor Theta(pi) has finite length and at most one irreducible quotient. For pi trivial, Theta(1) = S_v/R_v. Alternative (1) says that Theta(1) is irreducible or 0. Alternative (2) says that Theta(1) is generated by the class of s and that averages of translates by elements fixing s carry every class into the line of s; it implies that Theta(1) has at most one irreducible quotient, but it is a different condition, the one used by the Nakayama step of Lemma th-howe-tensor through Lemma th-howe-radical, where it replaces the finite length that the published theorem gives. The Lean also states the published theorem, as Published.HoweDualityUnitary, and derives from it at the inert places an analogue of Theorem lit-howe-duality-real (Published.HoweDualityFinite, by T.howe_duality_finite_of_unitary); that route (T.matched_maps_global_sum) is not the one followed here.
